# Canonical Systems Glossary {.unnumbered #sec-appendix-glossary}

This glossary provides the authoritative operational definitions for the foundational concepts of Physical AI. Each term represents a precise architectural invariant, physical boundary, or mathematical guarantee.

---

## Foundational Physical AI Architecture & Invariants

| Term                                                                                     | Operational Systems Definition                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            | Primary Reference                                 |
|:-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|:----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|:--------------------------------------------------|
| **Physical AI System**                                                                   | An autonomous computational system that couples unspecifiable learned neural policies to real-time physical actuators, exercising delegated authority over continuous matter, momentum, and thermodynamic energy under nonzero mass and finite latency.                                                                                                                                                   | @sec-boundary                                     |
| **Causal Boundary**                                                                      | The physical and temporal threshold at the memory-mapped actuator register write (DAC, PWM capture/compare latch, gate-driver control word) where digital bits are irreversibly transformed into physical energy, momentum, or thermal heat. Beyond this boundary, computational errors cannot be undone by software rollback.                                                                            | @sec-boundary                                     |
| **Endogenous Sensory Distribution Shift**                                                | The fundamental closed-loop feedback phenomenon where a machine's own physical actions modify the external environment, thereby reshaping its own future sensor distribution ($s_{t+1} \sim P(\cdot \mid s_t, a_t)$). A single policy deviation alters all subsequent observations, causing compounding quadratic error ($O(T^2 \epsilon)$) under behavioral cloning.                                     | @sec-boundary, @sec-data, @sec-training           |
| **Proposal–Permission Privilege Boundary**                                               | The architectural separation of privilege establishing that learned models (System 2 / MPU) generate unverified candidate proposals ($u_{\text{prop}}$), while an independent, deterministic supervisor (System 1 / MCU) running at $1000\text{ Hz}$ retains exclusive authority to permit, project, or veto execution.                                                                                   | @sec-boundary, @sec-brain, @sec-enforcement       |
| **Two-Speed Embodied Compute Architecture**                                              | An asymmetric compute topology partitioning a machine into a high-TDP, stochastic deliberative tier (1–50 Hz on Linux/accelerators) for semantic reasoning and perception, and a hard real-time, deterministic tier (1000 Hz on bare-metal MCU/FPGA) for closed-loop barrier enforcement.                                                                                                                 | @sec-brain, @sec-placement                        |
| **Expiring Intent Lease**                                                                | A strictly typed, time-bounded contract ($\langle \mathcal{G}, \tau_{\text{expire}}, \mathcal{E}_{\text{tol}} \rangle$) issued by the cognitive tier defining a spatial target envelope. An intent lease carries its own expiration deadline; if not renewed by the Brain before expiry, the real-time nervous system treats silence as an automatic fail-safe trigger and initiates controlled stopping. | @sec-intent, @sec-planning                        |
| **Action Chunk Seam Discontinuity**                                                      | The $C^0$ velocity or acceleration mismatch occurring at the boundary between successive multi-step receding-horizon trajectory chunks ($\hat{u}_{t:t+H}$). Splicing unblended chunks transmits destructive impulsive torque spikes ($\tau = J_{\text{eff}} \frac{\Delta\dot{q}}{T_c}$) through gearboxes, necessitating $C^2$ quintic polynomial blending.                                               | @sec-planning                                     |
| **Minimal-Intervention Safety Shield**                                                   | A real-time optimization filter that evaluates candidate neural actions at $1000\text{ Hz}$ via Control Barrier Functions (CBF). When a proposal threatens forward invariance ($h(x) < 0$), the shield solves a microsecond Quadratic Program (QP) that projects the command onto the boundary of the safe set ($\partial \mathcal{C}$) with minimal deviation from the user's intended heading.          | @sec-enforcement                                  |
| **Multidimensional Sim-to-Real Reality Gap Vector ($\boldsymbol{\Delta}_{\text{gap}}$)** | The coupled vector of physical discrepancies between simulation and reality across dynamics ($\Delta_{\text{dyn}}$), sensor transduction ($\Delta_{\text{sens}}$), visual appearance ($\Delta_{\text{vis}}$), and compute/transport latency ($\Delta_{\text{lat}}$). It cannot be collapsed into an abstract scalar.                                                                                      | @sec-training                                     |
| **Observational Indistinguishability Limit**                                             | The physical epistemic horizon where two distinct world states (one benign, one fatal) generate mathematically identical sensor telemetry prior to the braking deadline ($y_A(t) \equiv y_B(t)$ for $t \le t_{\text{deadline}}$). Once crossed, no downstream compute or neural architecture can differentiate the states in time to prevent physical harm.                                               | @sec-frontier                                     |
| **Astronomical Exposure Wall (Butler & Finelli Bound)**                                  | The mathematical theorem proving that certifying life-critical autonomous systems ($10^{-9}\text{ failures/h}$) purely through empirical fleet testing requires unfeasible testing durations ($>3.0 \times 10^9\text{ hours} \approx 342{,}000\text{ machine-years}$). High assurance must be achieved through deterministic architectural containment rather than accumulated road hours.                | @sec-evaluation, @sec-verification, @sec-frontier |

## Real-Time Silicon & Nervous System Mechanics

| Term                                                     | Operational Systems Definition                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      | Primary Reference                              |
|:---------------------------------------------------------|:----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|:-----------------------------------------------|
| **Lock-Free Seqlock Buffer**                             | A Single-Producer Single-Consumer (SPSC) shared-memory synchronization protocol utilizing an atomic monotonic sequence counter. Writers increment the counter before and after copying data; readers check parity before and after reading to detect torn writes without ever blocking the real-time execution path.                                | @sec-nervous, @sec-placement                   |
| **Worst-Case Execution Time (WCET)**                     | The provable upper bound on the time required for a software task to execute on target hardware ($R = C \cdot \frac{f_0}{f_1} + B + I_{\text{bus}} \le D$), accounting for core downclocking, interrupt blocking, and memory crossbar bus contention.                                                                                               | @sec-nervous, @sec-placement                   |
| **Zero-Allocation SRAM Invariant**                       | The architectural rule strictly prohibiting dynamic heap memory allocation (`malloc`, `free`, garbage collection) on the hard real-time safety path. All data buffers, active-set QP matrices, and ring structures must be statically allocated in on-chip SRAM/TCM to eliminate non-deterministic timing spikes.                                   | @sec-nervous, @sec-enforcement, @sec-placement |
| **Spatial Information Age ($\tau_{\text{age}}$)**        | The total physical duration elapsed between the midpoint of sensor optical exposure ($t_{\text{exp}}/2$) and the instant the resulting actuator command produces physical torque ($\tau_{\text{age}} = \frac{t_{\text{exp}}}{2} + t_{\text{readout}} + t_{\text{ISP}} + t_{\text{DMA}} + t_{\text{infer}} + t_{\text{enforce}} + t_{\text{rise}}$). | @sec-body, @sec-perception                     |
| **Belief State Invalidation Horizon ($t_{\text{exp}}$)** | The finite duration over which an unobserved state estimate remains within acceptable task tolerance ($t_{\text{exp}} = \inf \{ t \ge 0 : E(t) \ge E_{\max} \}$). Governed by physical drift rates and external disturbance acceleration.                                                                                                           | @sec-memory                                    |
| **Volumetric Free-Space Raycasting**                     | The process of casting negative-evidence sightlines through 3D spatial occupancy structures (TSDF, Sparse VDB) to clear previously occupied voxels. Prevents phantom obstacle persistence while tracking dynamic obstacles.                                                                                                                         | @sec-memory                                    |
| **Frozen Transform Trap**                                | A failure mode where an intermediate software transport bridge republishes cached spatial coordinate matrices ($T_A^B$) with updated wall-clock timestamps, misleading downstream nodes into treating stale spatial geometry as fresh telemetry.                                                                                                    | @sec-memory                                    |

## Robotics, Safety Assurance & Statutory Standards

| Term                                              | Operational Systems Definition                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                | Primary Reference                          |
|:--------------------------------------------------|:----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|:-------------------------------------------|
| **Dynamic Stopping Distance ($d_{\text{stop}}$)** | The total physical clearance required to bring a moving mass to a complete halt ($d_{\text{stop}}(v) = v \cdot \tau_{\text{latency}} + \frac{v^2}{2 a_{\max}} + \delta_{\text{margin}}$), combining linear reaction latency displacement with quadratic braking travel.                                                                       | @sec-body, @sec-enforcement                |
| **Inevitable Collision State (ICS)**              | A physical state $(x, v)$ from which no admissible control trajectory exists that can prevent a collision with obstacles or environment boundaries, given the robot's finite acceleration limits $a_{\max}$.                                                                                                                                  | @sec-body, @sec-planning, @sec-enforcement |
| **Dynamic Fallback Ladder (MRM)**                 | A 4-tier structured escalation protocol executed by the real-time supervisor when anomalies occur: Level 1 (Minimal Intervention QP), Level 2 (Category 2 Position Hold), Level 3 (Category 1 Controlled Dynamic Stop), Level 4 (Category 0 Safe Torque Off with spring-applied mechanical brakes).                                           | @sec-enforcement, @sec-intervention        |
| **Category 0 Stop (IEC 60204-1)**                 | An uncontrolled emergency stop achieved by immediately disconnecting electrical power to machine actuators, allowing gravity or spring-applied friction brakes to dissipate energy.                                                                                                                                                           | @sec-body, @sec-enforcement                |
| **Category 1 Stop (IEC 60204-1)**                 | A controlled stop where power is maintained to actuators to execute a maximum-deceleration dynamic brake trajectory until standstill, followed by complete power cutoff.                                                                                                                                                                      | @sec-body, @sec-enforcement                |
| **Category 2 Stop (IEC 60204-1)**                 | A controlled stop where power remains continuously supplied to machine actuators to maintain an active position hold against external gravity or process loads.                                                                                                                                                                               | @sec-body, @sec-enforcement                |
| **Envelope Trichotomy**                           | The formal safety case principle partitioning runtime state queries into *known-true* (verified safe, permit action), *known-false* (boundary breach, immediate trip), and *unknown* (epistemic uncertainty, sensor dropout). Crucially, **unknown must be treated as strictly outside the envelope**, triggering immediate degraded control. | @sec-release                               |
| **Claim-Argument-Evidence (CAE)**                 | A formal assurance framework structuring safety cases: top-level claims are broken down into logical sub-arguments supported by empirical test evidence from hardware-in-the-loop and in-situ fault injection records.                                                                                                                        | @sec-release                               |
| **Residual-Claims Register**                      | An auditable engineering ledger documenting every operational claim that cannot be empirically verified by testing or proven by software contracts, binding each residual risk to active mechanical containment and accountable human ownership.                                                                                              | @sec-frontier                              |
| **Detectorless Failure Mode**                     | A catastrophic physical failure mechanism that produces no detectable change in electronic telemetry before physical damage occurs (e.g., thermal rotor demagnetization, subsurface gear pitting, piezoresistive sensor diaphragm fatigue). Requires physical proof-testing rather than software monitoring.                                  | @sec-frontier                              |
| **Covariate Shift Flywheel**                      | The vicious cycle in imitation learning where compounding execution errors push the robot into unfamiliar states outside demonstration support, triggering larger errors that steer the machine directly toward hazards ($O(T^2 \epsilon)$ error accumulation).                                                                               | @sec-data, @sec-training                   |
| **Demonstration Provenance Tuple**                | The 4-stream action logging protocol $(a_{\text{req}}, a_{\text{cmd}}, a_{\text{enf}}, a_{\text{meas}})$ that distinguishes intentional human teleop commands ($a_{\text{req}}$) from kinematic transformations ($a_{\text{cmd}}$), safety governor clamps ($a_{\text{enf}}$), and structural compliance/backlash ($a_{\text{meas}}$).        | @sec-data                                  |
